3. Your Top 3 Bottlenecks

#1

Key-Person Risk

1/5

Four of five key-person risk areas flagged critical. Client onboarding stalls, key accounts go unfollowed, critical processes have single points of failure, and decisions pile up when the wrong person is out. With only 15% of processes documented, this isn't a perception — it's a structural vulnerability baked into how the company operates.

Why it matters: This is the Owner Trap at full scale. You can't build a Playbook Library when the playbooks live in people's heads. Every new SDR you hire faces the same painful onboarding you already experienced. Every departure is a knowledge evacuation — and in a 6-15 person team, losing one person means losing 10-15% of institutional knowledge overnight.

What good looks like: Where you are: knowledge locked in 2-3 people, no documented handoff processes, 15% documentation. Where you could be: Critical Client Flow mapped end-to-end, Department Champions assigned for each function, any team member able to cover a critical role for a full month.

Estimated annual cost: $80,000/year — based on 2 disruption events annually across 4 risk areas at your revenue level. Each event costs roughly a week of paralyzed productivity and delayed revenue.

#2

Founder Dependency

2/5

Deals fall through the cracks a few times a month, and your weekly health check is the bank account — a lagging indicator that shows you what happened, not what's happening. Your team is 'probably' aligned on priorities, which means the people closest to your customers may be rowing in a slightly different direction than leadership intends.

Why it matters: At $1M-$3M revenue, each lost enterprise deal can easily exceed $10K. Twenty-four dropped deals per year isn't a sales execution problem — it's a Visibility Gap. You're steering the business using the rearview mirror while your competitors have a live Scorecard on the dashboard.

What good looks like: Where you are: bank account as health check, deals slipping between handoffs, team 'probably' aligned. Where you could be: a weekly Scorecard with pipeline velocity, automated follow-up sequences that prevent any deal from going cold, and every team member able to name the same top 3 Rocks.

Estimated annual cost: $240,000/year — approximately 24 dropped deals at an average deal value of $10,000 for your revenue range and industry.

#3

Revenue Leakage

2/5

Your team burns 15-30 hours weekly on admin across 7-10 platforms. Despite having HubSpot and Sales Navigator, lead qualification and follow-ups — the exact task you'd snap-automate — remain manual. Your past Instantly campaigns and the painful SDR onboarding confirm the core issue: the process isn't documented well enough to delegate, let alone automate.

Why it matters: At your loaded hourly rate, that admin waste alone costs more than a full-time hire. But the real price is opportunity cost — every hour spent on manual data entry or chasing follow-ups is an hour not spent closing enterprise partnerships or improving the product that Tripadvisor and Unity already trust.

What good looks like: Where you are: 15-30 hours/week of manual admin, SDRs can't ramp without hand-holding, Instantly campaigns built ad-hoc. Where you could be: automated lead scoring from HubSpot + Sales Navigator data, sequenced follow-ups triggered by prospect behavior, and a documented qualification Playbook any new hire can follow from day one.

Estimated annual cost: $51,480/year — 22 hours/week × $45/hour × 52 weeks of admin work that should be systematized.

5. Your Automation Quick Win

You said: "Lead qualification and outreach follow-ups — we lose too many warm leads because nobody follows up fast enough"

Your instinct is spot-on — lead qualification and outreach follow-ups are your highest-leverage automation target. You already have HubSpot and Instantly in your stack, plus LinkedIn Sales Navigator for prospecting data. The gap isn't tools — it's the system connecting them. A documented lead scoring model fed by HubSpot activity data, connected to automated follow-up sequences in Instantly, could recover 10+ hours per week immediately and cut your dropped-deal rate in half. Based on your admin hours and deal frequency, systematizing this single workflow could save $120K+ annually — and finally make SDR onboarding painless.

Your current tools: HubSpot, Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Instantly, Calendly

6. Your Scalability Snapshot

If you doubled: "Operations would collapse"

You said operations would collapse if you doubled — and your track record confirms it. Tech adoption has been 'rocky,' and your SDR hiring attempt failed specifically because there was no documented playbook to hand over. The pattern is clear: your growth is people-dependent, not systems-dependent. You've tried to solve this with tools (Instantly) and people (SDRs), but without documented processes, both approaches hit the same wall. Companies at your stage that successfully scale invest in the Playbook Library first — documented, repeatable processes that anyone can follow — then layer automation on top. The encouraging news: your product-market fit and partner roster (Tripadvisor, Unity, Playtika) prove the demand is there. The bottleneck isn't the product. It's the operating system running the company behind it.

Past attempts: "Built some Instantly campaigns for cold outreach. Tried hiring SDRs but onboarding them was painful — no documented playbook for lead qualification."
